Prior to the cooperative wildlife management agreements, Crescent Land and Timber personnel were aware of the game potential in the Keowee-Toxaway forests where, for all practical purposes, the big game population was practically non-existent. Thus, enhancement of wildlife populations and their habitats was prepared years ago during the first phase of the Keowee-Toxaway Project and it has been continuing over the years in coordination with the forest management programs to increase timber production.
No comment required.
Crescent's forest harvesting operations require the fertilizing and seeding of logging roads and log landings to grass and lespedeza subsequent to logging operations which benefits wildlife as well as reducing soil erosion. Thus, the applicant is continuing an intensive mitigation program.
No comment required.
Duke does not think further studies of the distribution of rare or endangered species in the general project area are warranted at this time. However, when other projects are planned, Duke will undertake thorough investigations of the flora and fauna of those project sites.
No comment required.
9.5 Archaeology
Page 9-5
Applicant will conduct an archaeological survey along the line corridor where road construction and tower sites require grading.
See revised Section 9.5.
